dynamic_rules.effect: The SELECT picker chooses office groups defined in Setup > Office Groups (for example regions) instead of offices; when no office groups are defined, a group run covers all offices of the account. Cross-cutting statement of the document for all Lists screens (vendor articles on office groups and on the new reports menu) - recorded once here; it applies to every report of this category that has the Office / Office Group radios (all except Patient's Notes).
dynamic_rules.evidence_quote: `Office Group` picks groups defined in `Setup > Office Groups` (for example regions); without groups a group run covers all offices of the account.

corrections.text: The number in the office box is not a fixed default: with the Office radio the box defaults to the current office (the OID of the session, the same number the title bar shows) and SELECT picks other offices. Recorded once here; it applies to the office box of every report of this category (all except Patient's Notes).

APPOINTMENT DATE RANGE (Start Date / End Date) is matched on the appointment date: the report lists patients of a converted practice who have appointments in the range and whose insurance still needs to be updated.
corrections.evidence_quote: lists patients with appointments in the date range whose

corrections.text: PATIENT TYPE (Both / General / Ortho) is a row filter on the orthodontic status of the patient: the vendor article on listing all orthodontic patients uses PATIENT TYPE = Ortho. That the filter reads the Ortho Patient checkbox of the patient record (and not the patient-type tags of INCLUDE / EXCLUDE PATIENT TYPE) is the document's assumption - see unresolved.
corrections.evidence_quote: `PATIENT TYPE` `Both` / `General` / `Ortho` | Row filter on the ortho flag `[P55]`.

corrections.text: PATIENT STATUS (Active / Inactive / Both) replaces the checkbox Include Inactive Patients of the older screens (2014 criteria of Patient List - Detail): Active leaves inactive patients out. The same radio row sits on Patient List - Grouped By.
corrections.evidence_quote: `PATIENT STATUS` `Active` / `Inactive` / `Both` | Replaces the old checkbox `Include Inactive Patients`

corrections.text: INCLUDE PATIENT TYPE / EXCLUDE PATIENT TYPE filter on patient types: optional report tags of which a patient can carry up to six. Recorded once here; it applies to the same pickers on Patient List - Grouped By and Patients on Payment Plan.
corrections.evidence_quote: Patient types are optional report tags; a patient can carry up to six.

added_options.evidence_quote: `Patient List - New Patient` = `Appointment`, `Carrier`, `Created Date / First Visit Date`, `Referral`,
added_options.notes: Collapsed REPORT BY list, read by the research pass from a 2022 vendor screenshot of the opened dropdown. Complete list in the order given: Appointment (the default already in the inventory), Carrier, Created Date / First Visit Date, Referral, Referral Type - the fifth value is the next entry because the list wraps onto a second line of the document. Created Date / First Visit Date is ONE value whose name contains a slash; it is the legacy New Patient List (patient records newly created within the date range; the option name adds the second definition, first completed procedure). Referral = the legacy New Patients - By Referral (new records in the range, sorted by referral source). The meaning of Carrier (new patients by insurance carrier) is only inferred.

added_options.evidence_quote: `Referral Type` | `New Patients - By Referral Type` | New records in the range, sorted by referral type.
added_options.notes: Fifth and last value of the same REPORT BY list (a row of the document's REPORT BY table, which is headed as read from the 2022 vendor screenshot). Legacy report New Patients - By Referral Type: new records in the range, sorted by referral type.

corrections.text: REPORT BY = Appointment (the captured default; legacy report New Patient Thru Appointment) lists patients who have only a "New Patient" appointment and have not been activated into a full patient record - scheduler placeholders, not patient records.
corrections.evidence_quote: Patients who have only a "New Patient" appointment and have not been activated into a full patient record.

corrections.text: The value Created Date / First Visit Date names the two report definitions of a new patient: Created Date = the date the record was entered; First Visit Date = the first date a procedure was posted as completed. (How the screen lets the user choose between the two dates is not visible - see unresolved.)
corrections.evidence_quote: Two report definitions: `Created Date` (date the record was entered) and `First Visit Date` (first date a procedure was posted as completed).

added_options.evidence_quote: `Patient List - Grouped By` = 13 values (`Attached to Provider`, `Birthdate`, `Carrier`, `Employer`,
added_options.notes: Collapsed REPORT BY list of 13 values, read by the research pass from vendor screenshots of the opened dropdown (2022 and 2023). Order as listed: Attached to Provider (the default already in the inventory), Birthdate, Carrier, Employer, Fee Schedule, HIPAA Agreement, Insurance Plan, Last Visit, Medical Alert, Patient Type, Preferred Provider, Uninsured, Zip Code - three entries because the list wraps over three lines of the document. Birthdate = legacy Patients by Birthdate (list sorted by birthday month). Carrier = legacy Patients by Carrier (patients attached to a carrier). Employer = patients by employer of the insurance plan (meaning partly inferred).

added_options.evidence_quote: `Fee Schedule`, `HIPAA Agreement`, `Insurance Plan`, `Last Visit`, `Medical Alert`, `Patient Type`,
added_options.notes: Second line of the same 13-value REPORT BY list. Fee Schedule = legacy Patients by Fee Schedule (patients with their default fee schedule). HIPAA Agreement = who is and is not flagged as having a HIPAA agreement on file. Insurance Plan = legacy Patients Insurance List (plan assigned to each patient record). Last Visit = legacy Patients by Lastvisit (patients with their Last Visit date; used to find patients not seen for a period) - this mode changes the criteria panel, see the added controls and rules. Medical Alert = legacy Patients with Medical Alerts (patients having selected medical alerts). Patient Type = legacy Patients by Patient Type (patients per patient type, when one is set).

Third line of the same 13-value REPORT BY list. Preferred Provider = legacy Patients by Provider / Patients by Preferred Provider (patients assigned to a preferred provider). Uninsured = legacy UnInsured Patient List (patients without insurance; meaning partly inferred). Zip Code = legacy Patients by Zip Code (list sorted by zip code).

The PROVIDER and SPECIALTY sections of the default mode are replaced and no longer shown.

added_controls.evidence_quote: `Send Statement Status` | `Responsible Party-Send Statement Status` | Accounts eligible / ineligible to receive a statement | Date range replaced by `SEND STATEMENT STATUS` (`Yes` / `No`); `EXCLUDE RESPONSIBLE PARTY TYPE`; inactive-accounts checkbox
added_controls.notes: Appears only when REPORT BY = Send Statement Status, where it takes the place of CREATED DATE RANGE (our capture shows the default mode, Created Date). Read by the research pass from a 2023 vendor screenshot of that mode; the document calls it a dropdown. It filters on the Send Statement flag of the responsible party; documented use: choose No before a statement run to list the accounts that will get no statement. Default not documented.

added_options.evidence_quote: `Responsible Party List` = `Balance`, `Balance Aged Over X Days`,
added_options.notes: Collapsed REPORT BY list of six values, taken by the research pass from the vendor article on listing responsible parties. Order as listed: Balance, Balance Aged Over X Days, Created Date (the default already in the inventory), Resp. Party Type, Send Statement Status, Zip - two entries because the list wraps onto a second line of the document. Balance = legacy Responsible Party List by Balance (which accounts have a balance). Balance Aged Over X Days = legacy Responsible Party List Over [30/60/90/120] days (accounts overdue in the selected aging period). The default Created Date = legacy Responsible Party List (number of responsible-party accounts).

Send Statement Status = legacy Responsible Party-Send Statement Status (accounts eligible / ineligible to receive a statement) - this mode changes the criteria panel, see the added control and rule. dynamic_rules.effect: The CREATED DATE RANGE section is replaced by a SEND STATEMENT STATUS dropdown (Yes / No); EXCLUDE RESPONSIBLE PARTY TYPE and the inactive-accounts checkbox (Include Inactive Accounts (All patients inactive in account)) stay.
dynamic_rules.evidence_quote: Date range replaced by `SEND STATEMENT STATUS` (`Yes` / `No`); `EXCLUDE RESPONSIBLE PARTY TYPE`; inactive-accounts checkbox

corrections.text: The responsible party type is the account's billing type: every account has exactly one, and it is mandatory (examples: Cash, Collections, Discount Plan, No Type Defined).
corrections.evidence_quote: Exactly one mandatory type per account (billing type; examples `Cash`, `Collections`, `Discount Plan`, `No Type Defined`).

corrections.text: The single Statement Date identifies the statement run: the report lists the accounts for which a statement was generated on that statement date, so it has to equal the date of the run.
corrections.evidence_quote: After statements are generated, lists the accounts for which a statement was generated on a given statement
